title: MovieReaper Gives Hackers 21 Commands to Steal and Manipulate Files on Windows PCs
content_md: A newly identified malware framework named MovieReaper is spreading through malicious torrent downloads disguised as popular movies. The modular Windows threat gives attackers 21 remote file-management commands, enabling them to steal, inspect, alter, and delete data from infected systems. Researchers identified the campaign in mid-August 2026 after finding victims in multiple countries, including Russia, Türkiye, Japan, Kenya, Uganda, Colombia, Spain, the Netherlands, Belgium, and Germany. The operation has affected individual users as well as organizations in government, IT, consulting, retail, transportation, agriculture, and enterprise sectors . The threat is detected by Kaspersky products as HEUR:Trojan.Win64.Agent.gen . MovieReaper Grants File Control MovieReaper operators did not need to compromise torrent-tracker websites directly. Instead, they reportedly compromised itorrents[.]org , a public torrent-file repository used by several trackers. When users select a magnet link, the affected archive may return a malicious torrent file instead of the expected movie or software download. The torrent then downloads a loader disguised as a media release, such as the odyssey (2026) [1080p] [webrip] [5.1].exe . The initial file uses long names and familiar application icons to make the .exe extension less noticeable.
